## Rate limits

Per endpoint group (path + method groups).

More on limitsLess

Per-organization limit is 3x the per-API-key limit (the docs' 20 RPS per key = 60 RPS per org is an example, not a published value). Every 429 carries the RateLimit header (limit, remaining, reset seconds) and Retry-After; the old x-rate-limit-\* headers and body fields are documented as replaced. Some endpoints have stricter, unpredictable limits. Live unauthenticated probe of GET /api/v1/me/ (2026-10-25) returned 'ratelimit: limit=100; remaining=100; reset=1' plus ratelimit-\* and x-ratelimit-limit '100, 100;w=1' headers, i.e. 100 requests per 1-second window on that group; authenticated per-key values are not published.

## How to get an API key

Close uses Basic auth. The steps below follow Close's own docs.

1.  Create a Close account. API access starts on the Solo plan.
2.  Settings > Developer > API Keys (scoped to a user/organization pair)
3.  Send it with every request: header: Authorization: Basic base64('<api\_key>:') (key as username, empty password); OAuth 2.0 bearer for apps; MCP also accepts headers Close-API-Key + Close-Scope.
4.  Make a first call: Create a lead (company) with nested contacts, addresses, custom fields. Keep the key in an environment variable, never in the command.
    
    ```
    curl -X POST "https://api.close.com/api/v1/lead/" \
      -u "$CLOSE_API_KEY:" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{}'
    ```

## Strengths and limits

### Where it fits

-   Inside-sales teams that call and email from the CRM
-   Change-data sync via the event log (30 days back) and filtered webhooks
-   Agent access via the remote MCP with read / write\_safe / write\_destructive scopes
-   Bulk edits/emails/sequences over a saved search (Smart View or Advanced Filtering query)

### Where it falls short

-   Account-based models: Close's top object is the Lead (a company) with contacts nested inside
-   Free usage: every plan is paid; 14-day free trial, no card, but signup requires a phone number and consent to calls/texts
-   Batch record creation: no batch create endpoint in the docs; bulk actions operate on existing leads

### Worth knowing

-   Rate limits are per endpoint group and per key, with the org cap at 3x a single key; per-key numbers are not published (an unauthenticated probe showed 100 per 1-second window on GET /me/), so read the RateLimit header and honour Retry-After on 429. Source: [developer.close.com/api/overview/rate-limits](https://developer.close.com/api/overview/rate-limits)
-   API keys use HTTP Basic with the key as username and an EMPTY password (note the trailing colon). Source: [developer.close.com/api/overview/api-key-authentication](https://developer.close.com/api/overview/api-key-authentication)
-   Webhook subscriptions silently stop after 3 days of failed delivery (auto-paused) and need an API call to resume. Source: [developer.close.com/api/resources/webhooks](https://developer.close.com/api/resources/webhooks)
-   Event log only goes back 30 days. Source: [developer.close.com/api/resources/events](https://developer.close.com/api/resources/events)
-   Only the Python (closeio-api) and Node.js (closeio-node) clients come from Close; the Ruby, PHP, C#, Elixir and Go libraries are community-built. Source: [developer.close.com/api/overview/api-clients](https://developer.close.com/api/overview/api-clients)

2 moreShow fewer

-   The OpenAPI spec (since 2026-04-06) is marked experimental: Advanced Filtering POST /data/search/ is missing, and create-lead/merge/export bodies are untyped, so use the per-endpoint docs pages for request fields. Source: [developer.close.com/api/overview/changelog/2026/4/6](https://developer.close.com/api/overview/changelog/2026/4/6)
-   enrich\_field via MCP needs the mcp.write\_destructive scope, and the REST call is synchronous and may time out on complex guidance. Source: [developer.close.com/mcp/tools](https://developer.close.com/mcp/tools); [developer.close.com/api/resources/field-enrichment](https://developer.close.com/api/resources/field-enrichment)

## Before you build

Four things to settle first, each read off Close's own pages.

-   **Confirm the API is on your plan**API access starts on the Solo plan. Free tier: No free plan.
    
-   **Keep the key out of your code**Basic auth. It is sent as: header: Authorization: Basic base64('<api\_key>:') (key as username, empty password); OAuth 2.0 bearer for apps; MCP also accepts headers Close-API-Key + Close-Scope.
    
-   **Design around the rate limit**Per endpoint group (path + method groups).
    
-   **Know the catch before you scale**Rate limits are per endpoint group and per key, with the org cap at 3x a single key; per-key numbers are not published (an unauthenticated probe showed 100 per 1-second window on GET /me/), so read the RateLimit header and honour Retry-After on 429. Source: [developer.close.com/api/overview/rate-limits](https://developer.close.com/api/overview/rate-limits)

All 12 endpointsFor developers: method, path, what it does and what it costs.

**Base URL:** `https://api.close.com/api/v1`

**Bulk and async:** Bulk actions (edit, delete, email, sequence subscription) over a query or Smart View; async exports. Source: [developer.close.com/api/resources/bulk-actions](https://developer.close.com/api/resources/bulk-actions)

**Webhooks:** Yes. POST /webhook/ with url + events\[{object\_type, action, extra\_filter}\]; response includes signature\_key, payloads signed with HMAC-SHA256 in the close-sig-hash header. Failed deliveries retried with exponential backoff (up to every 20 min) for up to 72 hours; subscription auto-paused (queue cleared) if all deliveries fail for 3 days or the max queue length is reached, admins are emailed, and it must be re-activated via API. Source: [developer.close.com/api/resources/webhooks](https://developer.close.com/api/resources/webhooks) (verified 2026-10-25)
